**Trader consensus has converged overwhelmingly on 28°C as the highest temperature recorded in Madrid on August 25, 2026, reflecting real-time AEMET observations and forecasts showing a daytime peak of 28–28.4°C under partly cloudy skies and moderate southwesterly winds.** 

This outcome aligns with current surface data from stations like Madrid Retiro and Aeropuerto, where afternoon readings reached but did not exceed that level amid a cooler air mass and increased cloud cover that limited solar heating. The value sits below the 1991–2020 climatological average high of ~31°C for the date, consistent with regional model guidance indicating suppressed maxima due to these synoptic conditions. 

Market-implied odds near 100% for 28°C incorporate the “wisdom of crowds” from capital at risk, while acknowledging residual uncertainty from final official verification or micro-site variations at the primary reporting station. New hourly updates from AEMET could still refine the precise maximum before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent AEMET guidance for Madrid on August 26 forecasts a maximum of 29°C under partly cloudy skies with light winds, yet the market splits nearly evenly between 29°C and 30°C outcomes because short-range ensemble models retain modest uncertainty around peak heating. Subtle differences in boundary-layer mixing, urban heat-island effects at the official Retiro station, and slight variations in incoming solar radiation or afternoon convection can easily add or subtract one degree. Historical late-August climatology centers near 31°C, but current steering patterns favor slightly cooler maritime air, keeping higher thresholds below 10% implied probability while underscoring how the final observed maximum will hinge on the 24–48-hour forecast updates from AEMET and ECMWF.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Active southerly flow and associated convective activity from a weakening tropical cyclone are the main drivers keeping market-implied odds clustered around 30–31 °C for Hong Kong’s maximum temperature on 27 August.** Hong Kong Observatory forecasts show a range of 27–32 °C with high rain probabilities and intervals of thunderstorms, which limit solar insolation and daytime heating. Traders appear to weigh the balance between brief clear spells allowing brief warming toward 32 °C and persistent cloud/rain favoring 30 °C or lower. Updated HKO guidance and afternoon radar trends over the next 48 hours will likely determine whether probabilities shift toward the upper or lower end of the current narrow distribution.
